mission: Corridor, alone, night cycle. Ben slides down the bulkhead until he is sitting on cold deck plates. He pulls up Gavran's resonance note on his datapad: 'We lacked the will or the trust to attempt it.' He has been reading it as 'we weren't brave enough.' He re-reads: 'We couldn't trust each other enough.' Different emphasis. Different problem.
why_now: The recognition in Scenes 1-2 has to translate into a concrete shift before Ch19's Sera/Kael payoffs can land. Ben cannot arrive at the Jedi outpost still reading the note the old way.
conflict: Ben's body finally admits what it has been carrying. Interiority crowds in — self-reproach, the Jacen recognition, the Desh sentence. Mara's voice arrives as pragmatist, not myth: stop wondering if you are worthy and figure out what works.
turning_point: The resonance note's emphasis shifts under Ben's eyes. 'Will or trust' becomes two problems, not one. The trust problem is the problem he has been avoiding. It is also the one he has any chance of solving.
opening_hook: Ben slides down the corridor bulkhead until he's sitting on the deck plates, legs stretched across the narrow passage — the first time on this trip he's let his body admit how tired he is
closing_hook: The resonance note in the Codex files. Gavran wrote: 'We lacked the will or the trust.' Ben has been reading this as 'we weren't brave enough.' He re-reads it now: 'We couldn't trust each other enough.' Different emphasis. Different problem. Maybe a different solution.
emotional_trajectory: Exhausted honesty -> memory of Mara -> the angle shift on the resonance note

stakes.personal: Ben moves one file from the archive folder to the open one
stakes.interpersonal: The memory of Mara as a different model of leadership — pragmatist, not icon
stakes.external: The resonance note becomes the shape of a possible solution

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — corridor, alone, night cycle
sensory_details: Cold deck plates through his trousers; the bulkhead's low vibration against his spine; the ship's ambient hum; the datapad on his knees with the Codex notes glowing; the memory of his mother's voice, pragmatic, not a Force-ghost but a sentence she would have said; the resonance note's emphasis rearranging on a second read
action_beats: Ben slides down the corridor bulkhead and sits on the cold deck plates, legs stretched across the narrow passage
Ben pulls up the Codex notes on his datapad and scrolls to Gavran's resonance annotation
Ben reads the note again — 'we lacked the will or the trust' — and the emphasis shifts under his eyes
notes: Mara must remain the pragmatist. No mystical visitation, no reassuring dream, no Force-ghost. A memory of how she would have said it. One short sentence, and move. This is a micro-turn, not a breakthrough — Ben has not yet committed to a different approach; he has moved one file from 'return later' to 'open.' Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate the Skywalker-trap framework in interiority. The scene is the physical ritual of being tired, the datapad, the second read. The shift happens silently.
